name: Roger Samuelsson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Roger Samuelsson is a Swedish entrepreneur who owns 68% of Switzerland-based SHL Medical, the world's largest maker of autoinjectors.
He moved to Taiwan in 1988 and cofounded the firm a year later, after several years shipping local goods including boxing gloves back to Sweden.
Swedish private equity firm EQT acquired a 31% stake in SHL Medical in 2020; it now owns 32%.
SHL Medical was a pioneer in autoinjectors for home administration of drugs and its customers include Novo Nordisk, Amgen and Pfizer.
Samuelsson also owns the 414-foot megayacht Octopus, previously owned by Microsoft cofounder Paul Allen (d. 2018).

name: Nick Caporella
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Nick Caporella is the chairman and CEO of National Beverage, which he founded in 1985; it's best known for its LaCroix brand of sparkling water.
The Pennsylvania native started out as a contractor and worked as the CEO of telecom firm Burnup & Sims before founding his soft drinks business.
He kickstarted National Beverage by buying soda brand Shasta, then later added LaCroix to the portfolio in 1996.
The Fort Lauderdale, Florida-based company, which trades under the ticker FIZZ, has faced increased competition from rivals like PepsiCo and other brands selling flavored fizzy water.
forbes_facts: Caporella got his first taste of success in construction, where he reportedly scraped together $250 for a down payment on a used dragline excavator in 1957.
Burnup & Sims acquired Caporella's contracting business in 1972, and he was tapped to become the CEO just four years later.

name: David Baszucki
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Wikidata (2025); SEC insider holdings (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
forbes_bio: David Baszucki is cofounder and CEO of Roblox, a social gaming platform that allows kids and teens to play games that are made by fellow gamers.
Roblox's 83 million daily active users spent more than 73 billion hours using the platform in 2024.
Players on the platform can buy a digital currency, Robux, which lets them purchase special items within games.
Robux purchases allow tween developers of games to earn money for their efforts. The company paid Roblox creators nearly $1 billion in 2024.

name: Atul Ruia
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun India (2015-2019)
forbes_bio: US-educated Atul Ruia parlayed his family's ailing textile empire into a major real estate player with interests in retail, commercial, residential and hospitality.
The bulk of his wealth is tied to listed mall operator The Phoenix Mills, which he chairs.
Phoenix Mills has malls across India in cities such as Ahmedabad, Indore, Lucknow, Chennai, Mumbai, Pune and Bangalore.
The company's hotel portfolio includes the Courtyard Marriott in Agra and the St. Regis in Mumbai.
Ruia retired as managing director of Phoenix Mills in 2019.
forbes_facts: He's not related to the Ruia family of Essar group.

name: Eugene Murtagh
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Eugene Murtagh founded building materials manufacturer Kingspan Group in 1965.
He owns about 15% of the Dublin- and London-listed company, which primarily sells insulation products for commercial and industrial projects.
Kingspan has grown through acquisitions and has 212 manufacturing facilities in some 80 countries, with revenue of over $8 billion billion in 2022.
Murtagh stepped down as chairman and non-executive director of Kingspan in 2021, succeeded by Jost Massenberg.
The Kingscourt, Ireland resident had five children with his wife Andrea, who died in 2014.
forbes_facts: He started Kingspan by building agricultural trailers behind his family's bar, Murtagh's.

name: Chen Kaixuan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Hurun China (2006-2026)
forbes_bio: Chen Kaixuan chairs Guangzhou-headquartered Liby Group.
Liby Group manufactures washing powder, washing detergent, washing soap, and washing liquid products.
Chen set up Liby with his brother, Chen Kaichen, in 1994.

name: Aneel Bhusri
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Aneel Bhusri cofounded the business software firm Workday together with Dave Duffield, the founder of PeopleSoft.
Bhusri stepped down from his role as co-chief executive in 2024, taking on an advisory position.
Bhusri started his career in the early 1990s at business software firm PeopleSoft, where he rose to become vice chairman.
He's a former Intel board member and managing partner at venture capital firm Greylock Partners; he's been on the Forbes Midas List six times since 2008.
He studied electrical engineering at Brown University and has an MBA from Stanford.
forbes_facts: Bhusri joined the Giving Pledge, a commitment by the world's wealthiest people to dedicate the majority of their wealth to philanthropy, in 2018.

name: Alberto Bombassei
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: Alberto Bombassei chairs Brembo, a global leader in high-performance braking technology.
Brembo's brakes can be found in Ferraris, Corvettes and Harley-Davidsons around the world.
Founded by Alberto's father Emilio, Brembo broke into the big leagues in 1975, when Enzo Ferrari asked Emilio to outfit his race cars.
Alberto became general manager of the company in 1976, managing director in 1984 and was chairman from 1993 to 2021.
He has transferred his shares in the publicly traded company to his children, Luca and Cristina, but maintains control over their 53.5% stake.

name: Hans Jakob Limbach
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025)
forbes_bio: Hans Jakob Limbach is the founder of Limbach group, one of Europe's largest operators of laboratories for medical testing and research.
He started the company with a single laboratory in Heidelberg and later acquired 30 independent laboratories.
Headquartered in Heidelberg, the Limbach group now boasts 300 clinical specialists and has more than 6,000 employees.

name: Mohammed Dewji
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Mohammed Dewji is the CEO of METL, a Tanzanian conglomerate founded by his father in the 1970s.
METL is active in textile manufacturing, flour milling, beverages and edible oils in eastern, southern and central Africa.
In additional to Tanzania, METL operates in 10 African countries including Uganda, Ethiopia and Kenya.
Dewji, Tanzania's only billionaire, signed the Giving Pledge in 2016, promising to donate at least half his fortune to philanthropic causes.
Dewji was reportedly kidnapped at gunpoint in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania in October 2018 and released after nine days.
forbes_facts: Dewji retired from Tanzania's parliament in early 2015 after completing two terms.
Dewji, who is known as Mo (short for Mohammed), launched Mo Cola several years ago to compete with Coca Cola.

name: G. Rajendran
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun India (2018-2019)
forbes_bio: G. Rajendran chairs privately held GRT Jewellers, which he founded in 1964 as GR Thangamaaligai.
The jewelry chain sells diamond, gold, platinum and silver jewelry mostly in south India.
His sons G.R. Ananthapadmanabhan and G.R. Radhakrishnan are managing directors at GRT Jewellers.
He also chairs the GRT Institute of Engineering and Technology located outside Chennai.
His group's hospitality arm has hotels and resorts across 14 cities in south India.
Its hotel arm is building a resort in Maldives
forbes_facts: Rajendran hails from a family of jewelers from Kumbakkonam in Tamil Nadu.
Thangamaaligai means gold castle in the Tamil language.
